name: Johnson-noise thermometer
summary: A primary thermometer from a resistor's own noise. Every stage is on paper; nothing is built or bought.

inputs: wall audit: 'a thermometer must be calibrated against a reference temperature'
outputs: law, quantity, inversion and its assumptions, each with how it is checked

gate.condition: every assumption names a check that can fail

tools.name: CHECKS.json
tools.role: named check techniques the stage uses

law.name: Johnson-Nyquist noise (fluctuation-dissipation)
law.form: <V^2> = 4 kB T integral Re Z(f) df; for a pure resistor 4 kB T R B
law.lineage: Johnson, Phys. Rev. 32, 97 (1928); Nyquist, Phys. Rev. 32, 110 (1928); Callen and Welton (1951) for the general theorem

spec.quantity: absolute thermodynamic temperature T of a resistor
spec.signal: the open-circuit noise voltage spectral density of that resistor
spec.inversion: T = S_V / (4 kB Re Z); kB = 1.380649e-23 J/K exactly since the 2019 SI redefinition

wall_assumptions.assumption: the resistor is in thermal equilibrium at one temperature
wall_assumptions.how_checked: two readings 10 minutes apart agree within the statistical interval
wall_assumptions.if_broken: the reading is a weighted average of gradients; flag UNCAL

wall_assumptions.assumption: Re Z is known across the band (pure R, or R with a known shunt C)
wall_assumptions.how_checked: measure Re Z(f) with the injected-tone sweep before each run
wall_assumptions.if_broken: band-edge bias; at 100 kOhm and 100 pF, Re Z falls 28 percent by 10 kHz

wall_assumptions.assumption: no excess (1/f or current) noise in the resistor
wall_assumptions.how_checked: metal-film part, no DC bias, and the PSD is flat across 1 to 10 kHz within its interval
wall_assumptions.if_broken: T reads high; drop the band or the part

wall_assumptions.assumption: classical limit, h f << kB T
wall_assumptions.how_checked: kB T / h is 6.2 THz at 300 K, 9 orders above the band

wall_assumptions.assumption: the two amplifier chains' noises are uncorrelated
wall_assumptions.how_checked: zero-correlation null: independent noise into each chain must cross-correlate to zero (new check zeronull)
wall_assumptions.if_broken: correlated amplifier noise reads as temperature; shield, separate grounds and supplies

wall_assumptions.assumption: no interference couples into both chains
wall_assumptions.how_checked: shorted-input cross spectrum (auto-zero) is flat and below 1e-4 of the signal
wall_assumptions.if_broken: mains and radio lines read as heat; reject lines, improve the shield

spec.fundamental_bound: statistical: dT/T about (1 + a) / sqrt(B t) for the cross-spectrum, with a the amplifier-to-resistor noise power ratio; 0.1 percent needs about 150 s at B = 9 kHz

stages.does_not_prove: A primary thermometer still rests on Re Z, the band and the gain being known; it removes only the need for a reference temperature.

outputs: a seeded twin of resistor, two chains, ADC and estimator
known-answer tests the hardware will repeat

gate.condition: the twin recovers a planted T within its own statistical interval at 250, 300 and 350 K

tools.name: ngspice
tools.role: noise and AC analysis of the front end
tools.lineage: Berkeley SPICE (Nagel and Pederson, 1973) through SPICE3f5

spec.model: R = 10 kOhm metal film in a shielded can; two independent JFET-input chains, gain about 2000 each, band-pass 1 to 10 kHz; a stereo 24-bit ADC at 48 kHz; cross-spectral density averaged with Welch segments; T from the mean cross PSD over the flat band divided by 4 kB Re Z and the measured gain
code: planned: jnt/twin.py (not written; the room meter is the built example)

noise_sources.name: op-amp voltage noise (each chain)
noise_sources.value: 5.1 nV/sqrt(Hz) at 1 kHz, OPA1642 typical (TI OPA1642 data sheet, Electrical Characteristics, Noise, sha256 00c3e052...); power ratio a = 5.1^2 / 12.87^2 = 0.157

noise_sources.name: op-amp current noise through R
noise_sources.value: 0.008 nV/sqrt(Hz) (0.8 fA/sqrt(Hz) at 1 kHz, OPA1642 typical, same data sheet); correlated between chains, negligible

noise_sources.name: ADC quantisation and input noise
noise_sources.formula: q / sqrt(12 fs/2) referred through the gain
noise_sources.value: below 0.1 nV/sqrt(Hz) at the input with gain 2000

noise_sources.name: kT/C on the input node
noise_sources.value: 12 uV rms at 30 pF; it is the same noise seen through the RC, so it enters through Re Z, not on top of it

bounds.name: statistical floor
bounds.value: 0.39 percent at 10 s, 0.16 percent at 60 s, 0.05 percent at 600 s (B = 9 kHz)

bounds.name: band-edge roll-off
bounds.formula: Re Z = R / (1 + (2 pi f R C)^2)
bounds.value: 1.6e-4 at 10 kHz with 10 kOhm and 20 pF; the reason R is 10 kOhm, not 100 kOhm

known_answer_tests.name: planted temperatures
known_answer_tests.truth: synthetic resistor noise at 250, 300 and 350 K through the twin chains

known_answer_tests.name: zero-correlation null
known_answer_tests.truth: independent noise into each chain, true cross power 0

stages.does_not_prove: A twin built from datasheet figures says what the design can reach; it says nothing about the parts on the bench.

outputs: chain, part choices and a budget where the resistor's own noise dominates

gate.condition: the resistor's noise is at least 80 percent of each chain's total input noise power

tools.name: ngspice
tools.role: noise and AC analysis of the front end
tools.lineage: Berkeley SPICE (Nagel and Pederson, 1973) through SPICE3f5

chain.part_or_device: 10 kOhm metal-film or thin-film resistor, 25 ppm/K or better, in a copper can on a short guarded lead
chain.key_spec: no DC current, no excess noise

chain.part_or_device: low-leakage analog switches or reed relays
chain.key_spec: selects resistor, short (auto-zero), reference resistor at the ice point (substitution), injected noise (known signal), DAC loopback

chain.part_or_device: JFET-input op-amp, gain about 40 then 50, each chain on its own battery and ground return
chain.key_spec: e_n near 5.1 nV/sqrt(Hz) at 1 kHz, i_n near 1 fA/sqrt(Hz)

chain.part_or_device: 2nd-order high-pass at 300 Hz, 4th-order low-pass at 20 kHz, then a digital flat-band window 1 to 10 kHz
chain.key_spec: flatness measured by injection, not assumed

chain.part_or_device: stereo 24-bit audio ADC (USB interface with line inputs, or an ADC board on the microcontroller)
chain.key_spec: channel crosstalk below -100 dB, measured by the null test

chain.part_or_device: a small tone at 12 kHz injected after the switch, outside the analysis band
chain.key_spec: tracks gain drift in both chains continuously (pilotpath)

noise_budget.share_of_total: 0.14 per chain; removed on average by cross-correlation, still costs averaging time
below 1e-6; the only correlated amplifier term

adc.enob_or_floor: the null test measures the true floor; datasheet ENOB not trusted

spec.margin_to_bound: the chain sits at (1 + a) = 1.16 times the statistical bound; a noiseless amplifier would cut dT/T by at most 14 percent at fixed time, or averaging time by about 25 percent, since time scales as (1 + a)^2

stages.does_not_prove: A paper budget ignores layout pickup, microphonics and part-to-part spread.

gate.condition: two clean builds from the locked inputs produce the same image hash
gate.metric: distinct image hashes from two builds

tools.name: Raspberry Pi Pico SDK and arm-none-eabi-gcc
Nix flake with a locked input set
tools.lineage: Dolstra, The Purely Functional Software Deployment Model (2006); reproducible-builds.org practice

spec.platform: host Python reading the USB ADC first; an RP2040-class microcontroller drives the switch matrix and pilot tone

toolchain.name: Nix flake (Python, NumPy, pico-sdk, arm-none-eabi-gcc)
toolchain.pinned: flake.lock commits; every receipt carries the code and image sha256

reproducible_build.method: fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, sorted inputs, no embedded paths or times
reproducible_build.check: build twice on two machines, compare sha256

self_tests.name: auto-zero
self_tests.method: switch to the shorted input each cycle; subtract its cross spectrum
self_tests.pass_condition: shorted-input cross PSD below 1e-4 of the resistor's

self_tests.name: loopback
self_tests.method: DAC output into both chains through a divider
self_tests.pass_condition: gain matches the last calibration within 0.1 percent

self_tests.name: known noise injection
self_tests.method: pseudo-random noise of known digital PSD through the divider
self_tests.pass_condition: PSD read back flat within 0.2 percent across the band

self_tests.name: zero-correlation null
self_tests.pass_condition: cross power reads zero within 2 sigma

self_tests.name: pilot tone
self_tests.method: 12 kHz tone tracked in both chains every block
self_tests.pass_condition: gain drift since calibration below 0.05 percent, else UNCAL

self_tests.name: UNCAL annunciator
self_tests.method: any failed test or expired record sets the flag in every receipt
self_tests.pass_condition: a planted failure sets the flag (tested)

stages.does_not_prove: Identical hashes show the build is reproducible, not that the code is right.

outputs: a calibration record: gain-bandwidth product, Re Z(f), R ratio, null floor, date, expiry

gate.condition: the ice-point reading, after calibration, equals 273.15 K within the combined uncertainty

tools.name: CHECKS.json
tools.role: named check techniques the stage uses

spec.method: substitution and ratio: the same resistor and chains read at the ice point and at the unknown; T_x = 273.15 K x (S_x / Re Z_x) / (S_ice / Re Z_ice). The gain cancels in the ratio (the pilot tone shows it held), so only the R ratio, measured with one DMM in ratio mode, enters

references.name: ice point (distilled water and crushed ice, stirred)
references.traceability: a realisation we make ourselves; 273.15 K within a few mK when made with care (from memory, moderate); no certificate

references.name: Boltzmann constant
references.traceability: exact by definition in the SI since 20 May 2019

references.name: DMM in resistance-ratio mode
references.traceability: none: the meter's own calibration is unknown; a ratio needs only linearity

references.name: sample clock
references.traceability: the ADC crystal, about 50 ppm (from memory); enters B linearly and cancels in the ratio

spec.honest_traceability: Primary in principle: the kelvin follows from kB, which is exact, so absolute T needs no reference temperature. In this build the gain and band are known only through our own injection, and the ice point is our own realisation, so receipts say PRIMARY only for the ratio method at stated uncertainty and UNCAL whenever the pilot or null test fails. Where it fits in our stack: once it passes stage 7, this instrument becomes the reference that the GPU timing thermometer and every thermistor in the field kits are calibrated against by substitution.

stages.does_not_prove: Agreement at one fixed point does not test linearity across the range.

outputs: readback of planted temperatures through the real front end, scored as bits lost and error against truth

gate.condition: each planted T (250, 300, 350 K) read back within 2 sigma, and the null reads zero within 2 sigma

spec.rig: a second audio interface's DAC synthesises Gaussian noise shaped to 4 kB T R for a planted T, through a precision divider into the switch matrix's injection port: digital to analog to digital

signals.name: planted 250, 300, 350 K
signals.truth: the digital PSD times the measured divider ratio

signals.name: a stepped T (300 to 350 K mid-run)

scoring.error_vs_truth: |T_est - T_planted| in sigma units, per planted value
scoring.bits_lost: per frequency bin, 1/2 log2(1 + S / |S_est - S|^2 of the PSD), ideal digital path minus the real path, same estimator as room/roundtrip.py

stages.does_not_prove: Synthesised noise tests the chain and estimator, not the resistor's own physics; only stage 6 and 8 test that.

outputs: readings in real, non-digital places under a preregistered protocol

gate.condition: field readings agree with a co-located reference probe within the combined uncertainty in at least 9 of 10 runs

sites: a stirred ice bath and a stirred room-temperature water bath (known answers)
room air beside a desk, shaded
soil at 10 cm under one of the author's trees, against a thermistor probe
the cambium side of a bark flap on a fallen limb (never a living cut)

protocol.prereg: a studyrun spec written and locked before the first field run (not written yet)
known_answers: the thermistor, itself calibrated against this instrument at the ice point and in a water bath
protocol.kill_condition: if field agreement is worse than the bath agreement by more than a factor of 3, the instrument is lab-only
controls: shorted-input reading at each site (pickup control)
a site swap: the probe read at the wrong site's log time

stages.does_not_prove: Agreement with a thermistor that was calibrated against this instrument is circular for absolute T; it tests stability, not truth. The bath and ice point carry the truth.
